text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: High tail latency observed for single-tenant customer 'Spectral' in prod. p99 elevated; streaming stalls reported. Paging oncall. thread_id=svc-rt-09, affected-region=us-west-2
jamie: I'm oncall — seeing the page. pulling metrics now.
ryan: p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 1.2s over last 5m for tenant=spectral-prod. streaming stall rate ~3.1% (baseline ~0.2%). error rate not high but client-side timeouts reported.
marta: looks like a lot of very long prefix requests from that tenant recently — high prefix length + concurrency -> KV cache churn. seeing many KV evictions in runtime logs.
jamie: agree. are requests hitting dedicated pool or shared?
marta: single-tenant dedicated pool. capacity shows nodes at 85-95% GPU utilization with frequent small bursts. KV cache miss rate jumped to 72%.
zoe: customer success reports they launched a batch job that fanouts prompts to many workers ~30m ago. customer-facing impact: several streaming responses slowed; a few timeouts and customer dashboard alerts. they're currently holding traffic but want us to mitigate asap.
leon: put a temporary on-call mitigation plan: (1) short-term throttle high-concurrency sessions, (2) enable fallback to smaller model variant for this tenant, (3) pin cache config to prefer prefix caching, (4) scale up dedicated pool if needed.
jamie: executing mitigation 1+2 now. will post commands and traces.
jamie: throttling policy: apply per-tenant concurrency cap = 12.
jamie: `redwood quota set --tenant spectral-prod --concurrency 12`
deploy-bot: deploy queued: change-quota-handler v2 -> canary on routing service (by jamie).
jamie: canary looks healthy. applying fallback route to model 'redwood-small-v1' for tenant spectral as emergency fallback.
marta: note: small model has lower KV memory footprint and should reduce eviction pressure. might increase token latency slightly but reduce p99.
jamie: `redwood route update --tenant spectral-prod --fallback redwood-small-v1 --immediate`
deploy-bot: route update applied to us-west-2 nodes.
ryan: after throttle+fallback, p95 dropped to 300ms and p99 to ~650ms within 90s. streaming stalls decreased to 0.6%. good progress.
zoe: letting customer know we applied fallback + rate limit; asking them to pause the fanout job. they're appreciative, want an ETA for full remediation.
leon: next steps: (A) investigate prompt characteristics causing prefix thrash, (B) tune KV cache eviction policy (increase TTL or reserve capacity for this tenant), (C) consider short-term autoscale of dedicated pool.
marta: digging into prompt patterns: many requests contain very long system messages + repeated delimiters; average prefix length jumped from 800 tokens to 4500 tokens for a subset. that's causing large KV entries and forcing eviction.
ryan: let's capture a sample (redacted) and run a local repro against runtime with KV tracing.
jamie: grabbing sample from logs (redacted)
jamie: ```
[redacted] user_id=svc:spectral user_prompt_len=4578 tokens session_id=abc123 prefix_hash=0x7f4a2d
...
```
marta: thanks. repro locally shows kVCACHE thrash when concurrent sessions >20 with these prefixes. we can increase per-tenant KV reservation from 256MB -> 1GB to mitigate but that requires rolling config to runtime and will affect memory pressure elsewhere.
ryan: immediate safer option: enable aggressive prefix summarization for this tenant in routing layer: keep only last 1024 tokens for KV caching.
jamie: `redwood config set --tenant spectral-prod prefer_prefix_truncate=1024`
deploy-bot: config change pushed to config service; runtime will pick up on next sync (~15s).
ryan: after truncation and fallback, p99 now ~520ms, stalls ~0.3%. telemetry shows fewer KV evictions.
zoe: customer confirms improved UX; they paused their job and asking whether we can avoid hitting them with the fallback later.
leon: plan for next hour: (1) monitor metrics for 30m, (2) implement short-term KV reservation if observed thrash resumes, (3) follow up with product on rate-limit thresholds and billing for heavy fanout jobs.
marta: I'll open a PR for a more robust per-tenant kv reservation config and an alert to detect prefix-length spikes.
jamie: creating incident summary and triage note for handoff.
jamie: Incident timeline:
- 1795556789 root alert: p99 spike detected for tenant spectral-prod, streaming stalls (3.1%)
- 1795556792 throttle applied (concurrency cap 12)
- 1795556798 fallback route to redwood-small-v1 (immediate)
- 1795556810 prefix truncate enabled (1024 tokens)
- 1795556825 observed p99 down to ~520ms, stalls ~0.3%

ryan: analysis notes to include in postmortem: unusual prompt pattern (very long system messages + repeated delimiters) + customer fanout created high concurrency -> KV cache eviction -> streaming stalls and tail latency. Root cause: workload shape + insufficient per-tenant guardrails.
zoe: CS note: Spectral will run an internal post (they introduced their fanout change without notice). They want us to advise on safe concurrency limits and recommend client-side streaming timeouts.
leon: action items (owners):
- marta: PR for per-tenant KV reservation + alerting (ETA 4h)
- jamie: write incident summary and customer-facing timeline (ETA 30m)
- ryan: run deeper root-cause load repro and propose autoscale thresholds (ETA 6h)
- zoe: coordinate customer communication and ask for their mitigation plan (ongoing)

marta: also propose adding a runtime config `max_prefix_tokens_cached` with default 2048 and per-tenant override. will add to RFC.
jamie: handoff: I'm going offline in 10m — leon will take post-incident owner until next rotation. tagging @leon as interim.
leon: taking over. will check metrics in 15m and post updates. thanks team. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: incident note: route changes + config toggles documented in deploy logs (runbook-ref: kv-cache-thrash).
jamie: closing active pager for now — please escalate if p99 climbs above 900ms again.
ryan: will keep tracing on and add temporary enhanced logging for tenant spectral.
leon: logging/traces will be saved to incident/1795556789 for postmortem.
zoe: customer confirmed they paused the job and appreciate the fast response. scheduling follow-up with them tomorrow.
jamie: thanks everyone, good mitigation.
leon: final check in 20m, then marking as mitigation-stable if metrics hold.
